plainTitle: New windows allowed, front entrance change refused at heritage house at 9 Drumsnab Road

sources.label: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning

whatIsProposed.text: The owner of 9 Drumsnab Road asked for a heritage permit to replace the original windows and to make the front entrance bigger, including the side windows, the window above the door and the door opening.

citations.quote: The applicant proposes to remove the existing original windows and to enlarge certain features of the entryway assembly, including the sidelights, transom window, and door opening.

whatIsProposed.text: The house is in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. Changes to the outside of a house in such a district need permission under the Ontario Heritage Act.

citations.quote: Permission is required under Section 42(1)1 of the Ontario Heritage Act to alter any part of a property other than the interior of any structure or building on the property within a heritage conservation district.

whatIsProposed.text: City Council approved the window part of the application and refused the front entrance part.

citations.quote: City Council approve the portion of the application to alter the windows of the designated heritage property at 9 Drumsnab Road
City Council refuse the portion of the application to alter the front entryway of the designated heritage property at 9 Drumsnab Road

why.text: The entrance would be made longer because the ground floor inside the house was lowered by about 45 centimetres to make the ceilings higher. A longer door would give a level entry.

citations.quote: The purpose of the alteration is to lengthen the door and sidelights to provide a level entry into the house because the ground floor had been lowered by approximately 45 centimetres to increase ceiling height in the principle first floor rooms.

why.text: The owner also wanted new windows partly to fit security glass.

citations.quote: laminated, tempered insulated glass units could be integrated into the window assembly for added security

why.text: Staff's opinion is that a longer entrance would throw off the proportions of the front of the house. They suggested the owner find a solution inside the house instead.

citations.quote: It is Heritage Planning's opinion that the elongation of the centrally featured entryway skews the proportions of the detailing on the front elevation of the residence.
It is recommended that the owner explore an interior solution instead.

why.text: The house was built in 1925-26 in the Georgian Revival style. The heritage district plan rates it as having citywide significance.

citations.quote: 9 Drumsnab Road is a Georgian Revival residence built in 1925-26
it is noteworthy for its overall quality and has citywide significance

whoIsAffected.text: The owner of 9 Drumsnab Road. The house is on the north side of Drumsnab Road, overlooking the Don River ravine, in Ward 11 (University-Rosedale).

citations.quote: It is situated on the north side of Drumsnab Road, an enclave on the southeast edge of the SRHCD overlooking the Don River ravine lands.
11 - University - Rosedale

whoIsAffected.text: City budget: staff say the original recommendations have no cost to the City this year or in future years.

citations.quote: City Planning confirms there are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The approved windows must follow the plans by Browne & Perry Joinery Co. that were attached to a later staff report dated June 23, 2026.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: That later report is not summarized here, so this page does not describe what the approved windows look like.

citations.quote: in accordance with the plans submitted by Browne & Perry Joinery Co., attached as Attachment 1 to the revised supplementary report (June 23, 2026) from the Chief Planner and Executive Director, City Planning.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: If the owner appeals the refusal of the entrance change, City lawyers and staff will go to the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing to oppose the appeal.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The record does not say whether an appeal was filed.

citations.quote: City Council direct the City Solicitor and the appropriate City staff to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing to oppose the appeal.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: City Council put off its decision twice, in April and in May 2026, before deciding in June.

citations.quote: City Council on April 22 and 23, 2026, deferred consideration of Item TE31.24 to the May 20, 21, and 22, 2026, meeting of City Council.
City Council on May 20 and 21, 2026, deferred consideration of Item TE31.24 to the June 24, 25, and 26, 2026, meeting of City Council.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The Toronto Preservation Board also looked at this item and made recommendations to City Council.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The City's item page does not say what the Preservation Board recommended.

citations.quote: At its meeting on February 11, 2026 the Toronto Preservation Board considered Item

staff.text: In January 2026, staff recommended refusing the whole application, both the windows and the entrance. A revised staff report from June 23, 2026 followed; City Council adopted its recommendations, which approved the windows and refused only the entrance.

citations.quote: City Council refuse the alterations to the designated heritage property at 9 Drumsnab Road, in accordance with Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act, for alterations including the replacement of windows and alteration to the entryway assembly
That City Council adopt the following recommendations in the revised supplementary report (June 23, 2026) from the Chief Planner and Executive Director, City Planning [TE31.24a]:

committee.text: Toronto and East York Community Council sent the item to City Council without making a recommendation.

citations.quote: The Toronto and East York Community Council forwards the Item to City Council without recommendation.

council.text: City Council approved the new windows and refused the front entrance change. The vote was 23 to 1.

citations.quote: City Council on June 24 and 25, 2026, adopted the following:
Yes: 23
No: 1

whatHappensNext.text: City Council has made its decision. The owner can appeal the refusal of the entrance change to the Ontario Land Tribunal.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not say whether the owner appealed or what happens with the windows work next.

citations.quote: If the owner appeals City Council’s decision to refuse the application to alter the entrance of the heritage property at 9 Drumsnab Road under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
